config.title: Animation & interaction design

intro.title: Animation & interaction design
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive button that changes color and size when clicked, using CSS animations. You will learn how to use React state to track user interactions and trigger visual changes. The main technologies involved are React's useState hook for state management and CSS transitions for smooth animations. By the end, you will understand how to connect user events to dynamic styles to create engaging UI components.
intro.usecase: Animation and interaction design is essential for creating engaging user experiences in modern web applications. You'll implement these patterns in product dashboards where data visualizations animate smoothly between states, in e-commerce filtering interfaces where selections trigger immediate visual feedback, and in mobile navigation menus that slide or fade with gesture responses. These techniques transform static interfaces into responsive systems that guide user attention and communicate state changes intuitively. Mastering these skills allows you to build professional applications that feel polished and responsive to user actions.

objectives: Implement CSS transitions to animate element properties on state changes
Apply CSS keyframe animations to create custom motion sequences
Configure JavaScript event listeners to trigger interactive animations
Manipulate DOM elements with JavaScript to create dynamic visual feedback
Integrate animation timing functions to control movement acceleration
Construct interactive UI components that respond to user input with animations
Update element styles programmatically to create smooth state transitions

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. The component should return a single <div> element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'App' and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you defined a function named App that returns a <div>.

steps.title: Initialize animation state
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'isAnimating' initialized to false.
steps.hint: Call useState(false) and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a toggle state
const [isOn, setIsOn] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable to track whether animation should be active.
successCriteria: The App component contains a useState call that declares 'isAnimating' with initial value false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using useState with false as the initial value and naming the variable 'isAnimating'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to call useState(false) inside the component and name the first element 'isAnimating'.

steps.title: Define toggle animation handler
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named toggleAnimation that toggles the isAnimating state value.
steps.hint: Use the setter function from useState to update the state to the opposite of its current value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleAnimation function is defined that toggles the isAnimating state between true and false.
successCriteria: The toggleAnimation function is defined and uses setIsAnimating to toggle the boolean state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function uses setIsAnimating to toggle the boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleAnimation function isn't defined correctly. It should toggle the isAnimating state.

steps.instruction: Add a conditional className to the box div that includes 'animate' when isAnimating is true.

steps.title: Add toggle button with click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the container div, after the animated box, with an onClick handler that calls the toggleAnimation function and displays the text 'Toggle Animation'.
steps.hint: Place the button JSX element as a sibling to the box div, using the onClick attribute to trigger your toggle handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding an interactive button
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Toggle Animation' appears below the animated box, and clicking it will trigger the toggleAnimation handler (to be defined in the next step).
successCriteria: Button element is present inside the container div
Button has onClick attribute calling toggleAnimation
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add status display
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element inside the container that displays 'Animation: Active' when isAnimating is true, otherwise 'Animation: Paused'.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to conditionally render the text based on the isAnimating state variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element will appear below the animated box showing the current animation status.
successCriteria: The paragraph element uses a ternary operator to display 'Animation: Active' when isAnimating is true and 'Animation: Paused' when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or doesn't conditionally display the animation status correctly.
